logical_model.summary: Logical design for datamodel, derived from the conceptual model. 19 entities carry 21 relationships: 1 associative entities resolve many-to-many relationships and 2 entities are identified through a parent. 0 entities required a surrogate identifier because no business key was recorded. Attributes are typed against abstract domains and carry no platform-specific length, precision or storage.

subject_areas.name: Customer and Sales
subject_areas.description: The demand side of the business: who buys, what they ordered, and how they paid. This is the commercial heart of the model and the most heavily connected part of the schema.

subject_areas.name: Product and Sourcing
subject_areas.description: The catalogue of sellable goods, how it is organised for browsing, who supplies it, and the promotional offers applied to it.

subject_areas.name: Inventory and Fulfilment
subject_areas.description: Where goods are physically held and how they reach the customer or come back. Covers stock positions per location, outbound shipments, and returned goods.

subject_areas.name: Workforce
subject_areas.description: The internal organisation. Employees are servicing accounts as sales representatives and are arranged in a reporting hierarchy within departments.

subject_areas.name: Geography
subject_areas.description: A shared three-level location hierarchy used as reference data by both customers and warehouses. It is not owned by any one business process.

subject_areas.name: Governance
subject_areas.description: Change tracking. Records that a data-modifying operation occurred, who performed it and when.

entities.name: Audit Entry
entities.description: A record that a data-modifying operation took place, capturing which record type was affected, what kind of change it was, who made it and when. It refers to other records by name rather than by a modelled relationship, so it stands apart from the rest of the model.

entities.name: City
entities.description: A populated place, the lowest level of the shared location hierarchy.

entities.name: Country
entities.description: A sovereign country, the top of the location hierarchy, held with a short standard code as well as a name.

entities.name: Customer
entities.description: A person or organisation that buys from the business. Customers carry a credit limit, which indicates that trade is extended on account rather than strictly prepaid, and a lifecycle status.

entities.name: Department
entities.description: An organisational unit that employees are assigned to.

entities.name: Employee
entities.description: A person employed by the business. Employees are organised in a management hierarchy and are the salespeople attributed to orders.

entities.name: Order Line
entities.description: One product on one order, at the price agreed at the time of ordering. It is identified by its position within the order rather than by a key of its own, which makes it dependent on the order for its existence.

entities.name: Payment
entities.description: Money received against an order, recorded with the method used and the date it was taken.

entities.name: Product
entities.description: An item the business sells. Products are catalogued, sourced from a supplier, priced, stocked in warehouses and may be promoted.

entities.name: Product Category
entities.description: A grouping used to organise the catalogue for browsing and reporting. The structure is flat, with no sub-categories.

entities.name: Product Promotion Association
entities.description: Resolves the many-to-many relationship between Product and Promotion. Each occurrence records that one Product is promoted by one Promotion.

entities.name: Product Return
entities.description: Goods sent back by a customer after an order, recorded with the reason given.

entities.name: Promotion
entities.description: A discount offer applied to a set of products, expressed as a percentage reduction.

entities.name: Sales Order
entities.description: A customer's request to buy goods. The central transaction of the business: it links the buyer, the salesperson, the goods ordered, the money received, the dispatch, and any return.

entities.name: Shipment
entities.description: A dispatch of goods from a warehouse to fulfil an order, carrying a tracking reference that lets the customer follow it.

entities.name: State
entities.description: A state or province, the middle level of the location hierarchy.

entities.name: Stock Level
entities.description: How much of one product is held at one warehouse, together with the threshold at which it should be replenished. This is a business fact in its own right rather than a simple link, because it carries measures the business acts on.

entities.name: Supplier
entities.description: An external organisation that provides goods to the business, held with a named contact and direct contact details.

entities.name: Warehouse
entities.description: A physical location where goods are held and from which orders are dispatched.

normalization_actions.action: Resolved many-to-many between Product and Promotion
normalization_actions.rationale: A many-to-many relationship cannot be represented without a repeating group. An associative entity keyed on both parents removes the repetition and gives the relationship a place to carry its own attributes later.

normalization_actions.action: Checked non-key attributes against the full composite key
normalization_actions.rationale: Order Line has a composite key, so every non-key attribute (Quantity Ordered, Agreed Unit Price) must depend on the whole key rather than part of it. No partial dependency was found.

normalization_actions.action: Identified Order Line as dependent on Sales Order
normalization_actions.rationale: Its business key includes Sales Order's key (Order Number), so it cannot be identified independently. The relationship is identifying and the key is propagated rather than duplicated.

normalization_actions.action: Checked non-key attributes against the full composite key
normalization_actions.rationale: Stock Level has a composite key, so every non-key attribute (Quantity On Hand, Reorder Level) must depend on the whole key rather than part of it. No partial dependency was found.

normalization_actions.action: Identified Stock Level as dependent on Product
normalization_actions.rationale: Its business key includes Product's key (Stock Keeping Unit), so it cannot be identified independently. The relationship is identifying and the key is propagated rather than duplicated.

normalization_actions.action: Identified Stock Level as dependent on Warehouse
normalization_actions.rationale: Its business key includes Warehouse's key (Warehouse Name), so it cannot be identified independently. The relationship is identifying and the key is propagated rather than duplicated.

normalization_actions.action: Confirmed State attributes are not repeated on City
normalization_actions.rationale: City references State, which references Country. The chain is already decomposed, so Country's attributes reach City by navigation rather than by duplication.
